title: Medellin plane crash of 1935
summary: Two Ford Trimotor aircraft collided at Olaya Herrera Airport in Medellín Colombia on June 24 1935. SACO F-31 was taking off with 13 occupants including Argentine tango singer Carlos Gardel when it suddenly started to swerve and lose control. The aircraft veered off the runway and collided with taxiing aircraft C-31 causing an explosion that engulfed both planes in flames. Investigation revealed strong lateral winds combined with runway surface irregularities caused F-31 to lose control.
probable_cause: Loss of control during takeoff due to strong lateral winds combined with runway surface irregularities resulting in collision with taxiing aircraft.

factors.evidence: strong lateral winds in combination with irregularities in the surface of the runway
SACO F-31 started to swerve before losing control with the left main landing gear leaving ground before rotation
aircraft veered off the runway and collided with taxiing aircraft C-31
explosion followed which engulfed both planes in flames

events.text: SACO F-31 scheduled takeoff from Olaya Herrera Airport in Medellín with crew and passengers including Carlos Gardel.
Aircraft F-31 started accelerating down the runway then suddenly started to swerve.
Aircraft veered off the runway and collided with taxiing aircraft C-31 Manizales.
Explosion engulfed both planes in flames with all passengers and crew on C-31 killed.
